premise.claim: Pod Ready flaps because the controller writes a kubelet-owned condition: the controller writes Ready, becomes a second writer, kubelet's status-manager cache diverges, and kubelet republishes the stale value on its 10s sync (issue #460).
premise.evidence: Mechanism proven at unit layer: base branch calls util.UpdatePodReadyCondition in addNotReadyKey/removeNotReadyKey (a second writer of kubelet-owned Ready). Harness-bites check: the PR's contract tests FAIL against buggy base (controller rewrites Ready) and PASS on the PR head. See results/L1-bites-buggy-base-fails.txt + results/L1-prhead-pass.txt. Live *symptom* (25-35ms stale republish) NOT reproduced: the ACK controller is blocked by a pre-existing legacy-data issue unrelated to this PR (5 leftover test RoleInstances carry restartPolicy="None" string, which v0.8.0 cannot unmarshal, breaking the RoleInstance watch for the whole cluster). Not-refuted, not a blocker. See results/L3-blocked-legacy-data.txt.

integration._note: Not needed: the readiness utils are pure status-transition logic over an in-memory Adapter; the unit layer fully decides every finding. No envtest layer was added because it would exercise nothing the unit layer does not.

findings.note: addNotReadyKey no longer writes Ready (only the gate). Fails on base (controller writes Ready=False), passes on PR. Bites confirmed.
removeNotReadyKey no longer writes Ready. Fails on base (controller writes Ready=True -> the stale-True republish root cause), passes on PR. Bites confirmed.

Remaining inplace callers (inplace_update.go updateCondition, roleinstance inplaceupdate.go updateInstanceReadyCondition) still write Ready=False via UpdatePodReadyCondition. PR body claims this is safe because a spec/label write follows in the same reconcile, forcing kubelet to re-sync and refresh its cache. Static trace CONFIRMS: onlyUpdateRevision calls updateInstanceReadyCondition then sets the revision-hash LABEL + UpdatePod in the same function; Update() calls updateCondition then updatePodInPlace (spec patch) in the same function. Justification holds. Residual risk = sub-second window between the status and spec API calls (far smaller than the readiness-utils case, which had NO accompanying spec write). Not a blocker.

KWOK stage fidelity: new pod-ready-blocked + gate-aware pod-ready. Static check: jq expressions match the existing pod-ready stage syntax; logic emulates kubelet (promote Ready=True only when no gate is False; flip Ready=False when any gate is False; strategic-merge preserves controller-owned gates). Documented missing-gate fidelity gap is acceptable (controller injects both gates at creation). Live KWOK verification needs the stress suite (not run here) — recommend author confirm stress/e2e green with the new stages.

Aggregation latency: consumers reading Pod Ready (e.g. node_binding.go isPodRunningAndReady) see Ready ~1s later on return-to-rotation (kubelet derivation cadence). This is the documented cost of the fix, not a regression. The flap itself (which WAS visible in RIS readyReplicas 1->0) is removed. Acceptable.

liveNote: L3 live flap repro was BLOCKED by a pre-existing cluster-state issue (5 leftover test RoleInstances with restartPolicy="None" string break the v0.8.0 RoleInstance watch cluster-wide; the controller never reconciles a freshly applied RBG). This is unrelated to PR #461. To attempt the live flap: delete/patch the 5 leftover RIs (default/nginx-cluster-*-*, pr433-test/test-rbg-worker-0) to unblock the watch, then apply the issue #460 Variant-A repro (RBG flap + kubectl get -w on the replacement pod) and watch for the 25-35ms Ready True->False->True republish. Only do this with explicit cluster-owner OK (the leftover RIs are not this session's resources).
